rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes Moses’ words as a plea not to destroy the people and himself.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه الدعاء والطلب، أي لا تهلكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people meant by the threatened destruction are those who died in the quake.
rows.anchor: والمراد القوم الذين ماتوا من الرجفة.

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad reads the question as an expression of alarm; Moses knew God would not punish one person for another’s sin, as in Jesus’ prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: المراد بالاستفهام استفهام استعظام كأنه يقول:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the fools as the seventy and says Israel is threatened because they demanded to see God openly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالسفهاء السبعون. والمعنى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial is God’s test and examination, which Moses attributes to God rather than himself.
rows.anchor: { إن هى إلا فتنتك } أي ما هذا إلا اختبارك وامتحانك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ wording follows Abraham’s: he assigns illness to himself and healing to God.
rows.anchor: فأضاف المرض إلى نفسه والشفاء إلى الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joshua likewise blamed his forgetting on Satan, illustrating the same rhetorical practice.
rows.anchor:
وقال يوشع:
ومآ أنسانيه إلا الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses learned to call the event God’s trial from God’s statement that He had tested the people after Moses left.
rows.anchor: وإنما استفاد ذلك موسى عليه السلام من قوله تعالى له:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On returning, Moses saw the calf set up for worship and lowing, and recognized the trial.
rows.anchor: رأى العجل منصوبا للعبادة وله خوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial misguides or guides whom God wills; al-Qurtubi calls this a rebuttal of the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: من تشآء وتهدي من تشآء } وهذا رد على القدرية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience is told to recall, alongside earlier covenant reminders in scripture, the covenant taken from servants on the primordial day.
rows.anchor: أي واذكر لهم مع ما سبق من تذكير المواثيق في كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls this a difficult verse that scholars have discussed in interpretation and implications.
rows.anchor: وقد تكلم العلماء في تأويلها وأحكامها،

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One group says God brought descendants forth from one another and creation showed His oneness, since every adult necessarily knows there is one Lord.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم: معنى الآية أن الله تعالى أخرج

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal treats God’s address as testimony and the response as confession, analogizing it to the heavens and earth answering willingly.
rows.anchor: ذهب إلى هذا القفال وأطنب.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God created the souls before the bodies and placed in them knowledge by which they understood His address.
rows.anchor: إنه سبحانه أخرج الأرواح قبل خلق الأجساد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says prophetic hadith gives another account: God brought forth bodily forms containing spirits from Adam’s back.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم غير هذين القولين

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the report Umar heard the Prophet explain that God extracted descendants from Adam, assigning one group to Paradise and one to Hell; each is enabled to do the deeds of its destination until death.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسأل عنها. فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar calls the Umar-to-Prophet report disconnected because Muslim ibn Yasar did not meet Umar.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: هذا حديث منقطع الإسناد لأن مسلم بن يسار لم يلق عمر.

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معين
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Maʿin says Muslim ibn Yasar is unknown and Nuʿaym ibn Rabiʿa is not known for transmitting knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال فيه يحيى بن معين: مسلم بن يسار لا يعرف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though that chain is weak, al-Qurtubi says the meaning is sound through many established routes from the Prophet via several Companions.
rows.anchor: لكن معنى هذا الحديث قد صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report al-Tirmidhi authenticates says Adam’s descendants were drawn from his back and marked by light; Adam recognized David and gave him forty years from his own lifespan.
rows.anchor: روى الترمذي وصححه عن أبي هريرة قال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Adam later denied giving David forty years, and his descendants inherited his denial and forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A version outside al-Tirmidhi adds that God ordered the covenant to be written and witnesses to be present.
rows.anchor: في غير الترمذي: فحينئذ أمر بالكتاب والشهود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another version describes descendants as unequal in condition; Adam asks why they were not made equal, and God says He intended to be thanked.
rows.anchor: في رواية: فرأى فيهم الضعيف والغني والفقير والذليل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Amr transmits the Prophet’s comparison that the descendants were taken from Adam’s back as hair is combed from a head.
rows.anchor: وروى عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says God gave them intellects like Solomon’s ant and took their acknowledgment that He alone is Lord and deity.
rows.anchor: وجعل الله لهم عقولا كنملة سليمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They accepted the covenant, were told that messengers would be sent, and testified for one another.
rows.anchor: وأعلمهم بأنه سيبعث إليهم الرسل فشهد بعضهم على بعض.

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kab says the seven heavens were witnesses and every person born through the end of time received the covenant.
rows.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب: وأشهد عليهم السموات السبع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas places the covenant at Batn Nuʿman, a valley beside Arafa.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ببطن نعمان، واد إلى جنب عرفة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas locates it at Rahba in India, where Adam descended.
rows.anchor: وروى عنه أن ذلك برهبا أرض بالهند

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, quoted by Yahya ibn Sallam, says Adam was sent down in India and every soul destined to exist was extracted from his back.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن سلام قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية:

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the extracted descendants were then returned to Adam’s loins.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى قال الحسن: ثم أعادهم في صلب آدم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi locates the covenant between Mecca and Taif.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: بين مكة والطائف.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi places it in the lowest heaven after Adam descended from Paradise; God drew white descendants from his right side for Paradise and black ones from his left for Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: في السماء الدنيا حين أهبط من الجنة إليها

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says every soul destined for Paradise emerged white and every soul destined for Hell emerged black.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: خرجت كل نفس مخلوقة للجنة بيضاء

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi poses the objection that God seems to punish people who have not sinned or punish them for what He decreed and led them to do.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي رحمه الله:

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi answers that human limits come from a superior commander while God is answerable to none; creatures cannot be analogized to the Creator, all acts belong to God, and human objections arise from natural sympathy and hope of praise or benefit.
rows.anchor: قلنا: لأن فوقه آمرا يأمره وناهيا ينهاه،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some restrict the covenant to certain descendants: the wording excludes Adam’s direct offspring, while the later excuse about fathers excludes people without idolatrous ancestors.
rows.anchor: فقيل: الآية خاصة لأنه تعالى قال: { من بني آدم من ظهورهم } فخرج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another restriction confines it to those who received the covenant through the tongues of prophets.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي مخصوصة فيمن أخذ عليه العهد على ألسنة الأنبياء.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Others say the covenant is general because everyone knows they began as a child who was fed and raised and must have a creator and governor.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل هي عامة لجميع الناس لأن كل أحد يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the general reading, witnessing oneself means recognizing a creator, and saying yes is an admission of what is incumbent on everyone.
rows.anchor: فهذا معنى { وأشهدهم على أنفسهم }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After people forgot their acknowledgment, God reminded them through prophets, culminating in the Prophet, to establish proof; the text cites the command to remind and says God then empowered him and established his religion on earth.
rows.anchor: فلما اعترف الخلق لله سبحانه بأنه الرب ثم ذهلوا عنه ذكرهم بأنبيائه

rows.speaker: الطرطوشي
rows.claim: Al-Tartushi says the covenant remains binding even when people do not remember it, like a divorce witnessed against someone who later forgets it.
rows.anchor: قال الطرطوشي: إن هذا العهد يلزم البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says children who die young enter Paradise through their first-covenant acknowledgment; the view that children of polytheists are in Paradise is correct despite disputed reports.
rows.anchor: وهذا القائل يقول: أطفال المشركين في الجنة، وهو الصحيح في الباب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, from their backs is an appositional specification of from the children of Adam; Adam is omitted because all are known to be his descendants and drawn from his back.
rows.anchor: من ظهورهم } بدل اشتمال من قوله { من بني آدم }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufan readers and Ibn Kathir read offspring in the singular, which can denote either one child or many.
rows.anchor: { ذريتهم } قرأ الكوفيون وابن كثير بالتوحيد وفتح التاء، وهي تقع للواحد والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular offspring can refer to one child, as in the prayer for good offspring that was answered with the birth of Yahya.
rows.anchor: هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular also denotes a plural in the phrase progeny of Adam, since no progeny is greater in number.
rows.anchor: ولا شيء أكثر من ذرية آدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about being descendants after earlier generations uses the singular word collectively for a plural.
rows.anchor: وقال: { وكنا ذرية من بعدهم } فهذا للجمع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use the plural because many successive generations came from Adam’s descendants, an immense number known only to God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون «ذرياتهم» بالجمع، لأن الذرية لما كانت تقع للواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi refers the explanation of bala to al-Baqara’s verse about whoever earns an evil deed.
rows.anchor: تقدم القول فيها في «البقرة» عند قوله: { بلى من كسب سيئة }

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads both so that you say and or you say with the third-person ya, matching the surrounding third-person wording.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو بالياء فيهما. ردهما على لفظ الغيبة

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: Other readers use second-person ta, matching the direct address and response earlier in the passage.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتاء فيهما ردوه على لفظ الخطاب المتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes the angels speakers of we testified: after people affirm, angels testify so they cannot later claim ignorance.
rows.anchor: ويكون «شهدنا» من قول الملائكة.

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi say God told the angels to witness the people’s confession, preventing their later excuse.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد والضحاك والسدي.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ubayy ibn Kab instead take we testified as the children of Adam saying God is their Lord and deity.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب: قوله «شهدنا» هو من قول «بني آدم»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also says the children witnessed for one another.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أشهد بعضهم على بعض فالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If angels speak, pause after bala; if Adam’s children speak, the pause is unsuitable because the purpose clause depends on God making them testify.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان ذلك من قول الملائكة فيوقف على «بلى» ولا يحسن الوقف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continued prophetic report compares descendants drawn from Adam to combing hair from the head, then has angels witness their affirmation so they cannot deny it later.
rows.anchor: أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذرياتهم كما يؤخذ بالمشط من الرأس

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī selects the second-person reading because its meaning is sound and most readers use it.
rows.anchor: قال مكي: وهو الاختيار لصحة معناه،

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abu Malik says we testified is spoken by God and the angels, who bear witness to the people’s admission; al-Suddi also transmitted this view.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو مالك، وروي عن السدي أيضا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being descendants after their forebears means that the later generations followed their example.
rows.anchor: { وكنا ذرية من بعدهم } أي اقتدينا بهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about destruction for falsehood implies God will not do this; imitation gives no excuse in affirming oneness.
rows.anchor: { أفتهلكنا بما فعل المبطلون } بمعنى: لست تفعل هذا. ولا عذر للمقلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God justly created many among jinn and humans for Hell, then describes their failures.
rows.anchor: أخبر تعالى أنه خلق للنار أهلا بعدله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts are like those of people who do not understand because they gain no benefit, neither reckoning reward nor fearing punishment.
rows.anchor: أي بمنزلة من لا يفقه لأنهم لا ينتفعون بها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes fail to perceive guidance and their ears fail to hear admonitions.
rows.anchor: و { أعين لا يبصرون بها } الهدى. و { آذان لا يسمعون بها } المواعظ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not deny that their senses perceive anything at all; al-Qurtubi had explained this under al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وليس الغرض نفي الإدراكات عن حواسهم جملة كما بيناه في «البقرة».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble cattle because their aim is eating and drinking, but are more astray since livestock recognize benefit and harm and follow their owner while these people do not.
rows.anchor: فهم كالأنعام أي همتهم الأكل والشرب، وهم أضل لأن الأنعام تبصر منافعها

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says cattle know God, whereas an unbeliever does not.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: الأنعام تعرف الله، والكافر لا يعرفه.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says cattle obey God, whereas an unbeliever does not.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأنعام مطيعة لله تعالى، والكافر غير مطيع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heedless are those who abandon reflection and turn away from Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: { أولئك هم الغافلون } أي تركوا التدبر وأعرضوا عن الجنة والنار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command enjoins exclusive worship and avoidance of polytheists and those who deviate.
rows.anchor: أمر بإخلاص العبادة لله، ومجانبة المشركين والملحدين.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil and other commentators report that the verse was revealed after a Muslim prayed using Rahman and Rahim, and a Meccan polytheist mocked the apparent invocation of two lords.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل وغيره من المفسرين: نزلت الآية في رجل من المسلمين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Reports in al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmit from Abu Hurayra that God has ninety-nine names, with wording differences between the books.
rows.anchor: جاء في كتاب الترمذي وسنن ابن ماجه وغيرهما حديث عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the detailed al-Tirmidhi report is not mass-transmitted; Abu Isa calls it strange and says it is known only through trustworthy Safwan ibn Salih.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية وذكر حديث الترمذي وذلك الحديث ليس بالمتواتر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi distinguishes the mass-transmitted core: God has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one, and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.
rows.anchor: وإنما المتواتر منه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enumerating the names means counting and memorizing them; al-Qurtubi discusses other proposed meanings elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «أحصاها» عدها وحفظها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says he discussed the report’s authentication and documented over two hundred names, including disputed ones, and thirty-two introductory chapters on their rulings.
rows.anchor: وذكرنا هناك تصحيح حديث الترمذي، وذكرنا من الأسماء ما اجتمع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debate over whether a name is the named entity or the act of naming was discussed in al-Asna.
rows.anchor: واختلف العلماء من هذا الباب في الاسم والمسمى،

rows.speaker: ابن الحصار
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hassar says the verse applies name both to God as the named one and to naming: God refers to the named, names to designations, and the pronouns return respectively to God and names.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الحصار: وفي هذه الآية وقوع الاسم على المسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi invokes the Prophet’s five-names report as an example supporting the distinction between God and His designations.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s statement that he has five names, including Muhammad and Ahmad, supports the preceding linguistic point.
rows.anchor: لي خمسة أسماء أنا محمد وأحمد

rows.speaker: أهل الحق
rows.claim: The people of truth hold that a name is the named entity or an attribute related to it, distinct from the act of naming.
rows.anchor: والذي يذهب إليه أهل الحق أن الاسم هو المسمى،

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi’s first position is that name and named are one, since otherwise God’s names would belong to something other than God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي عند كلامه على قوله تعالى { ولله الأسماء الحسنى }:

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A second position takes names to mean designations, since God is one while names is plural.
rows.anchor: الثاني قال آخرون: المراد به التسميات

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says interpreters agree that names here means designations; al-Baqillani explains the ninety-nine as designations for God’s diverse qualities, including attributes of essence and action.
rows.anchor: قلت ذكر ابن عطية في تفسيره أن الأسماء في الآية بمعنى التسميات إجماعا

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr explains the designations as expressions for God’s varied qualities, some referring to His essence and others to attributes connected to Him.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر في كتاب التمهيد: وتأويل قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A third position says the names mean attributes.
rows.anchor: الثالث قال آخرون منهم: ولله الصفات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls His names beautiful because they point to His oneness, generosity, mercy, and beneficence and sound beautiful to hearts and ears.
rows.anchor: سمى الله سبحانه أسماءه بالحسنى لأنها حسنة في الأسماع والقلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Husna may be a verbal noun used as an adjective, or an elided feminine superlative meaning best.
rows.anchor: والحسنى مصدر وصف به. ويجوز أن يقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it is an adjective for a non-rational plural, it stays singular, as in the cited phrases about other benefits and mountains singing with David.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأول أفرد كما أفرد وصف ما لا يعقل كما قال تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Call on God with the name that suits the request: ask the Merciful for mercy, the Wise for judgment, the Provider for provision, the Guide for guidance, and the Opener to open.
rows.anchor: أي اطلبوا منه بأسمائه فيطلب بكل اسم ما يليق به، تقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A general name can accompany a fitting request, while the all-encompassing name Allah includes every name.
rows.anchor: وإن دعوت بالأعم الأعظم فقلت: يا الله فهو متضمن لكل اسم.

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi cautions against pairing a name with an unsuitable request unless the intended sense fits, and says ordering supplication this way leads to sincerity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهكذا، رتب دعاءك تكن من المخلصين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi notes that supplication conditions were treated in al-Baqara and earlier in this sura.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في «البقرة» شرائط الدعاء، وفي هذه السورة أيضا.

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi includes names such as Completer of His light, Best of heirs, Best of plotters, Fourth of three, Sixth of five, the Good, and Teacher.
rows.anchor: أدخل القاضي أبو بكر ابن العربي عدة من الأسماء في أسمائه سبحانه،

rows.speaker: ابن الحصار
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hassar says Ibn al-Barjan included names such as the Clean, which had not appeared in scripture or Sunna.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الحصار: واقتدى في ذلك بابن برجان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects the claim that neither the Good nor the Clean occurs in transmitted sources: the Good is in Sahih Muslim and the Clean in al-Tirmidhi.
rows.anchor: قلت: أما ما ذكر من قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi introduces a report from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet used a supplication for help, victory, and favorable plotting.
rows.anchor: وخرج عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول في دعائه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted prayer asks God for help, victory, and a favorable plot; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: رب أعني ولا تعن علي وانصرني ولا تنصر علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that basis, it is permissible to invoke God as Best of plotters and ask Him to plot for the supplicant, not against him.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا جائز أن يقال: يا خير الماكرين امكر لي ولا تمكر علي.

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi distinguishes names that may be invoked, those that may name God but not be used in invocation, and those that may do neither, following al-Ashari.
rows.anchor: وما يجوز أن يسمى به ويدعى، وما يجوز أن يسمى به ولا يدعى، وما لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilhad means deviation or abandoning the proper course; the root also describes a grave recess because it lies to one side.
rows.anchor: الإلحاد: الميل وترك القصد يقال: ألحد الرجل في الدين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read in two forms, both treated as Arabic variants.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «يلحدون» لغتان والإلحاد يكون بثلاثة أوجه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first kind of deviation alters God’s names, as polytheists derived names of their idols from them.
rows.anchor: أحدها بالتغيير فيها كما فعله المشركون،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada identify the derivations of al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat from divine names as examples of this alteration.
rows.anchor: مناة من المنان قاله ابن عباس وقتادة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second kind of deviation is adding names to those God has given.
rows.anchor: الثاني بالزيادة فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third kind is subtracting names, as ignorant people do when inventing invocations with names or acts unfitting for God.
rows.anchor: الثالث بالنقصان منها كما يفعله الجهال

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi urges invoking only from the Quran and five canonical hadith books, which include the Muwatta, and warns against inventing personal prayers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «فحذار منها، ولا يدعون أحدكم إلا بما في كتاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding names amounts to anthropomorphism and subtracting them to negation; the sound path avoids both.
rows.anchor: الثانية معنى الزيادة في الأسماء التشبيه، والنقصان التعطيل.

rows.speaker: أهل الحق
rows.claim: The people of truth say religion follows a middle way, without anthropomorphism or negation of attributes.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال أهل الحق: إن ديننا طريق بين طريقين، لا بتشبيه ولا بتعطيل.

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن البوشنجي
rows.claim: Al-Bushanji defines monotheism as affirming an essence unlike other essences and not stripping it of attributes.
rows.anchor: وسئل الشيخ أبو الحسن البوشنجي عن التوحيد فقال: إثبات ذات

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets leaving those who deviate as leaving them without debate or confrontation and considers the instruction abrogated by fighting.
rows.anchor: فالآية على هذا منسوخة بالقتال قاله ابن زيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes leaving those who deviate a threat, as in the commands to leave the isolated man and to let people eat and enjoy themselves; al-Qurtubi says this is apparent because they will be recompensed.
rows.anchor: وهو الظاهر من الآية لقوله تعالى: { سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dab means customary pattern, a term al-Qurtubi says was discussed under al-Imran.
rows.anchor: الدأب العادة. وقد تقدم في «آل عمران».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says the pattern is punishment when souls are taken and in graves, like Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: أي العادة في تعذيبهم عند قبض الأرواح وفي القبور كعادة آل فرعون.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation compares these people’s killing and captivity with Pharaoh’s people drowning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى جوزي هؤلاء بالقتل والسبي كما جوزي آل فرعون بالغرق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains the punishment: people changed their conduct; Quraysh’s blessings included fertile land, abundance, security, and wellbeing.
rows.anchor: تعليل. أي هذا العقاب لأنهم غيروا وبدلوا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument is illustrated by the verse saying God made Mecca a secure sanctuary while people around it were snatched away.
rows.anchor: أولم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا ويتخطف الناس من حولهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the blessing as Muhammad among Quraysh: they disbelieved, he moved to Medina, and punishment came upon the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: نعمة الله عليهم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kab says these verses were nearest in time to the Quran’s descent from heaven; Said ibn Jubayr instead says the last revelation was the verse about returning to God.
rows.anchor: هاتان الآيتان في قول أبي أقرب القرآن بالسماء عهدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi reconciles the statements by suggesting Ubayy meant these verses were nearest to heaven after the verse about returning to God.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون قول أبي: أقرب القرآن بالسماء عهدا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority says the address is to Arabs, recalling the favor that a messenger came in their language, was understood by them, and gave them lasting honor.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للعرب في قول الجمهور، وهذا على جهة تعديد النعمة عليهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the address is to all people and means that a human messenger came to them; al-Qurtubi first calls the Arab reading more correct.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هي مخاطبة لجميع العالم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says every Arab tribe had a share in the Prophet’s birth, so the address means an Ismaelite messenger came to the Arabs.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما من قبيلة من العرب إلا ولدت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although he calls the Arab reading more correct, al-Qurtubi says the universal reading makes the proof stronger because the messenger is human like his audience and can be understood and followed.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني أوكد للحجة أي هو بشر مثلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From among yourselves praises the Prophet’s lineage as belonging to the core and purest Arab line.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { من أنفسكم } يقتضي مدحا لنسب النبي

rows.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
rows.claim: Wathila reports the Prophet saying God chose Kinana from Ishmael’s descendants, Quraysh from Kinana, Hashim from Quraysh, and the Prophet from Hashim.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن واثلة بن الأسقع قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says his ancestry came through lawful marriage, never fornication; al-Qurtubi explains there was no illicit conception back to Adam.
rows.anchor:
وروي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" إني من نكاح ولست من سفاح "

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن قسيط المكي
rows.claim: Ibn Qusayt al-Makki reads from yourselves with a fatḥa on fāʾ, deriving it from excellence; the reading is also reported from the Prophet and Fatima and means a most distinguished messenger.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن قسيط المكي من «أنفسكم» بفتح الفاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes from yourselves to mean from among the most obedient of you.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من أنفسكم أي أكثركم طاعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is grievous to the Prophet when his people are burdened; anat means hardship, as in a difficult and destructive steep slope.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { عزيز عليه ما عنتم } أي يعز عليه مشقتكم.

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the root of taʿannut is imposing severity: to make someone suffer is to constrain them with something hard to perform.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: أصل التعنت التشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi first treats ma as a verbal noun clause with a fronted predicate, then prefers the alternative that makes the phrase the subject of grievous and grievous an adjective of the Messenger.
rows.anchor: «عزيز» صفة للرسول، وهو أصوب.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the praise terms could also be read in the accusative as circumstantial descriptions.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: ولو قرىء عزيزا عليه ما عنتم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن داود الخريبي
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas calls this the best meaning consistent with Arabic usage, transmitting al-Khuraybi’s explanation that the Prophet is grieved if people enter Hell and keen for them to enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: وأحسن ما قيل في معناه مما يوافق كلام العرب
